examples.pie: gʰóstey h₁yós moysóns gʷr̥h₃ési. h₁yós-kʷe nos dʰrā́gʰm̥ píph₃esi. h₁yós nos str̥h₃méni légʰesi ḱludʰí nos. h₂én gʷh₂dʰí deywṓs toy h₁wésuh₂ h₂én dh₃ih₁ént.
examples.en: Guest, you who devour the rams, and you who drink our dregs, you who lie on our bed, hear us! Go over there; may the gods give you good things over there.

examples.pie: nu ph₃tóm h₂nérm̥ séngʷʰōmes. léymonm̥ péh₃t srowéh₂m-kʷe péh₃t. nu h₂usési h₂ew tr̥syéti. dʰwóri-kʷe h₂énti gʷéHyeti. nu gʷíh₃woyh₁t dʰrā́ks-kʷe h₁ésmōd mē lelikʷyéh₁t.
examples.en: Now let us sing of the drunken man. He drank the lake, and he drank the river. Then at dawn he thirsts again. And he sings in front of the door. Now may he live, and may the dregs not be gone from him!

examples.pie: gʰóstey trís h₂wést. príHe me trís h₂éles. túH h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr. gʷówes moy lelikʷḗr dʰrā́ks-kʷe lelóykʷe. nu toy h₂Hséh₂i h₁épi sísdōh₂. nu kʷid toy ne h₁ésti priHós-kʷe toy h₁ésti.
examples.en: Guest, it has dawned three times. Three times you fed me, friend. You are a giver of good things. My cattle are gone, and the dregs are gone. Then I will sit at your hearth. Now you have nothing, and you have a friend.

pie-lex-gjerh2onts.gloss: old, aged; as noun (m.): old man, elder

examples.en: Elder, what is salt? We bring salt from the salt marsh. We put it on the meat, and the meat becomes tasty. Give it to me!

examples.pie: bʰéh₂tu ǵérh₂onts werdʰom.

examples.pie: kʷíd swésor bʰúHt? méne bʰréh₂tēr pérwr̥ gʷéh₂t ne-kʷe nést. deywṓs h₁ím h₂léksōnti gʷémeti-kʷe.
examples.en: "Sister, what has happened?" "My brother went to the mountain and did not return." "The gods will protect him, and he will come."

examples.en: Neighbour, I bring you honey. Your honey is sweet! Take butter for your children. May your herd increase!

examples.en: Father, tonight I will guard the herd. You are bold, my son. Take the spear and the old dog. Do not sleep; sit by the fire. I will not sleep.

examples.en: Fame-from-the-Gods, tell me a story about the aurochs. A herdsman went into the forest. There he caught sight of a huge aurochs. The aurochs struck him with its horns. Did he die? He did not die: he climbed into a tree and slept there. At dawn he came home unharmed. That is a good story!

examples.pie: swésor káprōs pérwr̥ ḱnént. káprōs ne sn̥gʷént. péh₂uros upó trémti. upó stéygʰe h₁ím-kʷe ní wodʰéye. ne memógʰh₂e pérwr̥ bʰérǵʰu. nu stéygʰōh₂ bʰólǵʰim moy kapyé. swésor bʰebʰudʰdʰí. nu h₁mé próti gʷm̥yéti.

examples.en: Mother, when will a man lead me home? You are still young, daughter. Wait three summers. That is long! It is short. I waited five summers. And then my father arrived? He arrived with ten cows, and he led me home.
